transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I'm here because my manager at the restaurant told me I needed to see someone. I guess... what scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service. Or I'd just start doing things totally out of order. Like, the other day, I was just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers over and over instead of actually closing out the checks. I don't really know why I did it, but it freaked them out.
During that episode when you were standing there repeating table numbers, do you remember what was happening around you at the time, or is that time a blank to you now?

Um... I'm not really sure. It's mostly just a blank to me now. I mean, I know we were in the middle of a shift, so there must have been people moving around and talking, but... I don't actually remember seeing or hearing what anyone was doing right then. It's just kind of fuzzy.
After that episode ended, did you feel unusually drowsy, confused, or exhausted afterward, or did you feel like yourself again fairly quickly?

Um, no, not really. I didn't feel sleepy or exhausted or anything like that. I think I felt like myself again pretty fast. I was mostly just... confused about why my coworkers were staring at me. But physically, no, I felt fine right after.
Right before that episode started, did you notice any unusual warning signs—like a strange smell, taste, tingling, or a sudden wave of fear or deja vu?
Um... no, I don't think so. I didn't smell anything weird or feel tingly or anything like that. And I wasn't scared, either. It just kind of happened.

Have you noticed whether these episodes tend to happen during times of high stress, emotional conflict, or after something upsetting, or do they seem to occur randomly regardless of what's going on in your life?

Um... I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. They just seem to happen randomly. I mean, work can be stressful sometimes, obviously, but... no, I wouldn't say they only happen when I'm upset or stressed out. It just kind of comes out of nowhere, really.
During these episodes, have you or anyone else noticed you making repetitive movements like lip-smacking, chewing, swallowing, or fumbling with your hands or clothing?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that, and nobody at the restaurant has mentioned it to me either. I don't think I do any lip-smacking or chewing, or messing with my clothes. They just tell me I act strange or kind of freeze up, but... no, no repetitive movements that I know of.
During or after these episodes, have you or anyone else noticed any physical signs like biting your tongue, losing control of your bladder, or getting injured?
No, definitely not. Um, I haven't bitten my tongue or had any accidents like losing control of my bladder. And I haven't gotten hurt, either. So, no, nothing like that.
Has this happened more than once, and if so, about how many times has this occurred and over what period of time?

Um, honestly, I'm not entirely sure how many times it's happened. It's definitely been more than once, but... I haven't really kept a count or tracked how long it's been going on. I just know it's happened a few times.
Aside from these specific episodes, do you ever notice gaps in your memory for daily events, or times when you feel detached from yourself or like you're watching yourself from outside your body?
No, I don't really have gaps in my memory for normal, everyday stuff. And I've never felt like I was watching myself from the outside or detached like that. It's just the other things I mentioned.
Have you ever had a significant head injury, high fever with seizures as a child, or any family members with epilepsy or seizure disorders?

No, I've never had a bad head injury. Um, my parents never said anything about me having high fevers or seizures when I was little, either. And as far as I know, nobody in my family has epilepsy or any kind of seizure disorder. So, no, none of that.
During one of these episodes, if a coworker called your name or touched your arm, did you respond to them at all, or did you seem completely unreachable until it passed?

Um, from what they told me, I was pretty unreachable. What really scared everyone at work is that I would just start freezing up right in the middle of a busy service. Or I'd do things completely out of order... like, they said I was just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was repeating table numbers out loud instead of actually closing out the checks. So if someone called my name or tried to get my attention while I was like that, I didn't really respond to them at all.
Do you know roughly how long these episodes tend to last—are we talking about a minute or two, or could they go on for much longer, like ten minutes or more?

Um, I'm not entirely sure exactly how long they last, honestly. Since I'm kind of out of it when it happens, it's hard for me to keep track of time. My coworkers haven't really given me an exact number of minutes either, just that I'm standing there for a bit before I snap out of it. So I can't say for sure if it's just a minute or if it goes on longer.
When these episodes happen, do they tend to look basically the same each time—same kind of behavior and movements—or do they vary quite a bit from one episode to the next?

Um, I'm not really sure if they look exactly the same every time. I mean, since I'm not really aware of what I'm doing when it happens, I can't say for sure. My coworkers mentioned the time by the soda station, but they haven't really said if I do the exact same things every single time. So, I don't really know if it varies or not.
Have any of these episodes ever happened while you were asleep, or right as you were waking up?

Um, no, not that I know of. I mean, I live alone, so if it happens while I'm sleeping, there's nobody there to tell me about it. But as far as I know, it's only ever happened when I'm awake, like at work. I've never noticed anything weird right when I'm waking up, either.
During these episodes, do your eyes stay open, or do they close tightly, and if someone tried to open your eyelids, would they meet resistance?

Um, I really couldn't tell you. Like I said, I'm completely out of it when it happens, so I don't know what my eyes are doing. And no one at work has ever mentioned trying to pry my eyes open or anything like that. They just said I was standing there staring, so... I guess maybe they're open? But I don't know for sure.
Did any of your coworkers mention noticing any brief jerking, twitching, or shaking of your arms or legs, or any weakness on one side of your body, during or right after these episodes?

Um, no, they didn't say anything about that. They just said I was standing there, kind of frozen, I guess. Nobody mentioned any shaking or twitching, and I haven't felt weak on one side or anything like that afterwards. I just feel really tired and confused when I snap out of it.

Can you walk me through what was happening right before each episode you can recall—were you dealing with a particularly stressful table, a conflict with a coworker, or anything emotionally charged in the moments leading up to it?

Um, no, not really. I don't think so. I mean, it's a restaurant, so it's usually busy and there's always some level of stress, but... nothing out of the ordinary right before it happens. I wasn't arguing with anyone or dealing with a really bad customer. I was just doing my normal job, taking orders, running food... just regular stuff. There wasn't any big emotional thing right before.
